prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Sentinel Vale:ground-only land/coastal/cryosphere imagery;predictable latency,documented quality,retained external interfaces. Mission Control Center(Bluebell/local voice):safety,commands,passes,anomalies,routing,handover. Flight Dynamics Facility(Mistral/legacy logs):authoritative orbit catalog,accepted-solution assumptions;navigation,maneuvers,orbit/visibility/pointing→planning. Mission Planning System(Cedar):authoritative observation/contact timelines;booking(service,antenna,elevation,volume,priority);checks spacecraft/station/staffing conflicts,slew,sun-angle,power,thermal recovery,recorder,command-load,separation→command preparation package→Bluebell command engineering. Network Control System(Lantern):authoritative circuits/routing/allocations/readiness/contact records;antenna/link/timing/routing status→Bluebell. Ground Network Manager(Juniper/rosters):assignments,availability,conflicts,maintenance,staffing,site coordination;maintenance compatibility confirmation mandatory before preparation. Antenna Deicing Notice:mandatory maintenance-critical pre-acquisition tasks;Spacecraft Operations Team assesses contingency margin. North S-Band Antenna(nominal),South S-Band Antenna(procedure-compatible alternate):commands/low-rate telemetry→Bluebell;Kiruna X-Band Antenna,Svalbard X-Band Antenna:high-volume downlink;all supply quality/timing-qualified tracking. Command Validation Gateway(Osprey):mandatory independent pre-uplink validation before approval;syntax,timing,ranges,sequence,modes,baseline;rejects unapproved edits,missing provenance,expired configurations,out-of-window activities. Cybersecurity Desk reviews unusual-access/emergency-procedure/nonstandard-transfer exceptions. Mission Control Center+Spacecraft Operations Team concurrence required before command-stack queuing for authorized uplink. Telemetry Ingest Service:state→command checks;validated frames/contact/flow indicators→operations/engineering/processing;metadata,gaps/interruptions;Pass Replay Packet. Orbit Determination Engine:radiometric tracking,telemetry timing,force models,approved maneuvers→dynamic orbit solutions;qualified-pass Doppler Residual Report→Flight Dynamics Team:bias/model-error separation before acceptance. Product Quality Service:pre-distribution geometry/mode checks;each orbit solution:frame,covariance,time continuity,contact-prediction consistency. Continuous orbit control ensures common predicted trajectory. Maneuver screening:fuel,contacts,payload outages,post-burn tracking;Flight Dynamics Team computes candidate state

Document units:
S141: The Flight Dynamics Facility distributes routine ephemerides and event predictions through controlled interfaces used by the Mission Control Center, Mission Planning System, and Payload Processing Facility.
S142: The Mission Planning System uses accepted orbit files to align imaging requests, contact opportunities, recorder margins, and downlink windows.
S143: The Command Validation Gateway checks maneuver command parameters against the screened burn plan before allowing the command stack to proceed.
S144: The Flight Dynamics Team produces the Ephemeris Delta Note when updated state vectors change predicted acquisition times or imaging geometry beyond agreed thresholds.
S145: The Orbit Determination Engine produces the Laser Retroreflector Window from the refined orbit solution and the approved station geometry constraints.
S146: The Spacecraft Operations Team receives maneuver recommendations with enough lead time to rehearse commanding, verify contingency actions, and coordinate contact coverage.
S147: The Payload Calibration Team obtains predicted viewing geometry from flight dynamics products to interpret instrument trends and plan calibration activities.
S148: The Network Control System uses antenna pointing predictions derived from the accepted ephemeris to prepare scheduled contacts and verify tracking readiness.
S149: The Long Term Archive retains released orbit products, covariance data, maneuver records, and quality decisions so that later processing can reproduce the operational context.
S150: When the Primary Processing Cluster is unavailable, the Backup Processing Cluster supports product generation with the same validation checks and distribution rules.
S151: The Payload Processing Facility is responsible for transforming downlinked payload telemetry into image products that are traceable to the source telemetry and to the processing configuration used at execution time.
S152: Raw transfer starts when station delivery files arrive with an accompanying manifest, and the ingest workflow verifies file size, sequence continuity, checksum, and acquisition time before processing is scheduled.
S153: The Telemetry Ingest Service writes accepted raw data to immutable staging storage and records the session identifier used by downstream processors.
S154: Corrupted or incomplete raw segments are isolated from the nominal queue, and the operator display shows whether recovery, retransmission, or discard is required.
S155: The Primary Processing Cluster generates Level 0 products by removing transfer framing, ordering source packets, and preserving instrument time tags without radiometric or geometric correction.
S156: Level 1A processing reconstructs detector samples and appends engineering context, while Level 1B processing applies radiometric calibration and sensor model parameters.
S157: Level 2 processing applies geolocation, atmospheric screening where applicable, and gridding rules defined in the active product specification.
